Rashi on Menachot 91a:10:1.english: I would include the firstborn, (and the Paschal offering,) and the [animal] tithe, and the Paschal offering.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:11:1.hebrew: והשתא דכתיב עולה - ולא מצית לרבויי בכור ומעשר ופסח, והוי עולה גופה פרט, דהוי כלל ופרט וכלל: דועשיתם אשה לה' - כלל, עולה או זבח לפלא נדר או בנדבה - פרט, לעשות ריח ניחוח - חזר וכלל:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:11:1.english: And now that olah is written - And you cannot include the firstborn, [animal] tithe, and the Paschal offering; and the olah itself is [part of] the specification, so that it is a general statement, a specification, and a general statement: "And you make an offering by fire to the Lord" is a general statement; "a burnt offering or a sacrifice to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering" is the specification; "to make a pleasing aroma" is once again a general statement.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:11:2.hebrew: מאי מרבית ביה - דהואיל ואמרת אוציא חטאת ואשם, יש לך לומר: מה הפרט מפורש אף כל, ומאי נינהו דקאמר לרבויי מפרט זה:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:11:2.english: What do you include by it? - For since you said, "I will exclude a sin-offering and a guilt-offering," you must say: "Just as the specific detail is explicitly [defined], so too all [similar items are included]"; and what are they that it speaks of including from this specification?

Rashi on Menachot 91a:11:3.hebrew: שאין מחוייב ועומד - שאין מחוייב בעולה, דבעולת נדבה מיירי:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:11:3.english: That one is not already obligated - That one is not obligated to bring a burnt-offering, for [the verse] is dealing with a voluntary burnt-offering.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:12:1.hebrew: להביא ולדות של קדשים - נקבות של שאר קדשים, דעולה זכר [ולא שייך ולד]:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:12:1.english: To include the offspring of consecrated animals - [Offspring of] females of other consecrated offerings, for a burnt offering is male [and offspring is not applicable to it].

Rashi on Menachot 91a:12:2.english: And a burnt offering that comes from surplus [funds] - As we said earlier in our chapter (Menachot 90b).

Rashi on Menachot 91a:12:3.english: And their substitutes - That is, where he substituted [an animal for] the burnt offering.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:13:1.hebrew: ואשם שניתק לרעייה - ושחטו לשם עולה ולעשותו כליל כעולה, הילכך טעון נסכים:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:13:1.english: And a guilt offering that was relegated to pasture - And he slaughtered it for the sake of a burnt offering, and to make it entirely consumed like a burnt offering; therefore, it requires libations.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:13:2.hebrew: וכל הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן - שהן כשרים, אלא שלא עלו לבעלים, שטעונין נסכים:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:13:2.english: And all sacrifices that were slaughtered not for their designated purpose - That they are valid, except that they did not count for the owners [toward fulfilling their obligation], [to teach] that they require libations.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:14:1.hebrew: והשתא דאמרת או - מן הצאן אתי לדרשא לחלק, או דלפלא נדר או נדבה למה לי? לחלק איצטריך, דסד"א כו':
Rashi on Menachot 91a:14:1.english: And now that you say “or” - [That the “or” in “or] from the flock” comes for an exposition to divide: Why do I need the “or” of “to fulfill a vow or a freewill offering”? It was necessary to divide, for you might have thought, etc.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:15:1.hebrew: הניחא לרבי יאשיה - דאמר: אע"ג דלא כתיב יחדו, כמו דכתיב דמי, להכי איצטריך האי או לחלק:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:15:1.english: This works out well according to Rabbi Yoshiyah - Who said that even though “together” is not written, it is considered as though it were written; therefore, this “or” was needed to separate [them].

Rashi on Menachot 91a:16:1.hebrew: אי נמי איפכא - דאייתי שלמים בנדר, עולה בנדבה, בעי נסכים כל חד וחד:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:16:1.english: Or vice versa - That he brings a peace offering as a vow [and] a burnt offering as a freewill offering, each and every one requires libations.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:18:1.english: Or a sacrifice - Why do I need [the word] "or"?

Rashi on Menachot 91a:1:1.hebrew: הואיל דכתיב בויקרא ומן הצאן - כיון דהוה ליה למיכתב מן הצאן, וכתיב ומן, כמו דכתיב יחדו דמי. וגבי אביו ואמו, אע"ג דכתיב ואמו, לא משמע יחדו, משום דהתם לא אפשר בלא וי"ו, דהיכי ליכתוב? ומקלל אביו אמו – משמע אביו קילל אמו:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:1:1.english: Since it is written in Leviticus, “and from the flock” - Since it could have written “from the flock,” and [instead] it wrote “and from,” it is considered as though it wrote “together.” And regarding [the verse,] “his father and his mother,” even though it is written “and his mother,” it does not imply “together,” because there it was impossible without a vav. For how could it write? “One who curses his father his mother” would imply [that] his father cursed his mother.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:20:1.english: Or peace offerings - Why do I need [the word] “or”?

Rashi on Menachot 91a:22:1.hebrew: ורבי יאשיה - דנפקא ליה מיעוט עולת העוף מן הבקר, או למה לי? דבשלמא לרבי יונתן, דדריש האי או לחלק; ורבי יאשיה נפקא ליה לחלק מן ואם מן הצאן ומאם עולה קרבנו מן הבקר, ולמעוטי עולת העוף נפקא ליה ממן הבקר ומן הצאן:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:22:1.english: And Rabbi Yoshiya - Since he derives the exclusion of a bird burnt-offering from "of the herd," why do I need "or"? For it is well according to Rabbi Yonatan, who expounds this "or" to divide [the offerings]; but Rabbi Yoshiya derives [the rule] to divide from "And if from the flock" and from "If his offering is a burnt-offering of the herd," and to exclude a bird burnt-offering he derives from "of the herd" and "of the flock."

Rashi on Menachot 91a:23:1.hebrew: [בתרי מיני - הוא] דבעי נסכים לכל חד, בחד מן הצאן או בקר תסגי ליה כו':
Rashi on Menachot 91a:23:1.english: [With two kinds] - It is [in that case] that libations are required for each one; [whereas] with a single [kind, whether] of the flock or of the herd, it would be sufficient for him, etc.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:24:1.hebrew: ככה תעשו לאחד - דמשמע נמי לכל אחד נסכיו בפני עצמו, למה לי? והדר פירש דינו של כל אחד:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:24:1.english: So shall you do for each one - Which also implies that each one has its libations by itself. Why do I need [this], seeing that it then went back and specified the rule for each one?

Rashi on Menachot 91a:24:2.hebrew: אבל אייתי בבת אחת - נדר ונדבה, אימא תסגי וכו':
Rashi on Menachot 91a:24:2.english: But [if] he brought [them] at the same time - [Such as] a vow and a freewill offering, I might say it should suffice, etc.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:25:1.english: And three tenths [of an ephah] of fine flour for a meal-offering mixed with oil - It is written regarding a wealthy metzora.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:25:2.hebrew: במנחה הבאה עם הזבח - כלומר, שזקוקה לזבח שקריבה עמו:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:25:2.english: Regarding a meal offering that comes with the sacrifice - That is to say, that it is bound to the sacrifice, being offered with it.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:26:1.hebrew: או אינו אלא במנחה הבאה בפני עצמה - כלומר, שהמנחה אינה זקוקה לזבח, אלא מנחה בפני עצמה היא:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:26:1.english: Or perhaps it refers only to a meal offering that comes on its own - That is to say, that the meal offering is not tied to a sacrifice, but rather it is a meal offering on its own.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:27:1.english: And I still do not know whether they require wine libations or not - For wine is not explicitly written in it [the passage].

Rashi on Menachot 91a:27:2.hebrew: תלמוד לומר - בפרשת שלח: "ויין לנסך רביעית ההין וגו'". לא הוה צריך קרא למימר, דכבר כתיב בראש הפרשה "עולה או זבח". מה תלמוד לומר "על העולה או לזבח":
Rashi on Menachot 91a:27:2.english: The verse states - In the portion of Shelach: "And wine for the libation, a fourth of a hin, etc." Scripture did not need to state [this], as it is already written at the beginning of the passage, "a burnt offering or a sacrifice." Why [then] does the verse state, "with the burnt offering or for the sacrifice"?

Rashi on Menachot 91a:27:3.english: Rather, a burnt offering - This is the burnt offering of a leper.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:27:4.english: This is the leper's guilt offering - That all three of them require libations.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:28:1.hebrew: ותיפוק ליה תרוייהו - חטאת ואשם מזבח, ולא ליבעי קרא לכל חד וחד:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:28:1.english: And let both of them be derived - [Namely,] the sin-offering and the guilt-offering, from [the word] zevach, and let a verse not be required for each and every one.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:2:1.english: And according to Rabbi Yoshiya, who said: Even though "together" is not written, it is considered as if it were written - And this [phrase], "from the herd or from the flock," is needed by him to exclude a bird burnt-offering.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:2:2.hebrew: ליבעי קרא - לחלק, דרצה אחד מביא:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:2:2.english: A verse should be required - To divide [them, teaching] that if one wishes, he brings [only] one.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:3:1.english: But is it not written - [There is already] another verse to separate [them].

Rashi on Menachot 91a:3:2.english: If his offering is a burnt offering of the herd, and if his offering is of the flock, etc. - Which implies to divide [them].

Rashi on Menachot 91a:4:1.hebrew: ורבי יונתן אמר לך: אף ע"ג דכתיב אם עולה קרבנו מן הבקר, איצטריך ליה מן הבקר או מן הצאן לחלק:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:4:1.english: And Rabbi Yonatan [could] say to you: Even though it is written: “If his offering is a burnt offering of the herd,” he required [the verse] “of the herd or of the flock” to distinguish [between them].

Rashi on Menachot 91a:4:2.english: These words - That if he wishes, he may bring this [one].

Rashi on Menachot 91a:4:3.english: Where he specifies - At the time of the vow, [whether it is from the] flock or cattle.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:5:1.hebrew: תודה לאו זבח הוא - מהיכא דנפקי עולה ושלמים, מההוא נמי משמע תודה, למה לי לרבויי מאו:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:5:1.english: Is a thanksgiving offering not a sacrifice? - From where a burnt offering and peace offerings are derived, from that [same word] a thanksgiving offering is also implied; why do I need to include [it] from [the word] "or"?

Rashi on Menachot 91a:5:2.hebrew: הואיל ואתי לחם בהדה - ואינה חשובה זבח, לא ליבעי נסכים. אי נמי, משום דהוי הלחם במקום נסכים, (אי נמי) ליקום במקום נסכים:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:5:2.english: Since bread comes with it - And it is not considered an ordinary sacrifice, let it not require libations. Alternatively: Because the bread is in place of libations, (alternatively) let it stand in place of libations.

Rashi on Menachot 91a:8:1.hebrew: וליכתוב קרא לפלא נדר או בנדבה - ולא ליכתוב לא עולה ולא זבח, דכל שבא בנדר ובנדבה, דהיינו עולה ותודה ושלמים. ומנחה, דאין טעונה נסכים, מימעיט ממן הבקר או מן הצאן:
Rashi on Menachot 91a:8:1.english: And let Scripture write: "To fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering" - And let it write neither "burnt-offering" nor "sacrifice," for everything that comes as a vow or as a freewill offering—namely, a burnt-offering, a thanksgiving-offering, and peace-offerings—[would be included]. And a meal-offering, which does not require libations, is excluded by "from the herd or from the flock."

Tosafot on Menachot 91a:13:1.hebrew: וכל הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן - תימה: הא למה לי קרא? כיון דדרשינן בריש מכילתין (דף ב.): אם כמה שנדרת עשית יהא נדר, ואם לאו יהא נדבה - ליבעי נסכים כנדבה! וכי תימא דלגבי נסכים לא הוה מוקי ליה לקרא - הא על כרחיך צריך לאוקומי הכי, שאם אי אתה אומר כן פסלתו, כדאמר רבי יוחנן לעיל גבי אשם מצורע. ונראה, דכדי נסביה, משום דאי לאו קרא דמוצא שפתיך מהכא הוה נפקא ליה, ועיקר קרא לאחרינא אתא:
Tosafot on Menachot 91a:13:1.english: And all sacrifices that were slaughtered not for their own name - This is astonishing: why do I need a verse [for this]? Since we expound at the beginning of our tractate (2a): "If you did according to what you vowed, it shall be a vow [neder], and if not, it shall be a voluntary gift [nedavah]" - let it require libations like a voluntary gift! And if you were to say that regarding libations he would not apply the verse - behold, perforce one must apply it so, for if you do not say so, you would invalidate it, as Rabbi Yoḥanan said above regarding the guilt-offering of a leper. And it appears that [the Tanna] cited it incidentally, because had there not been the verse of "That which has gone out of your lips" (Deut. 23:24), it would have been derived from here; but the primary purpose of the verse came for the other [cases].

Tosafot on Menachot 91a:1:1.hebrew: הואיל וכתיב ומן הצאן כמאן דכתיב יחדו - דמדכתיב מן הבהמה והדר כתיב מן הבקר ומן הצאן, משמע שניהם (ובקונטרס פירש בע"א), דתרוייהו אפירושא דבהמה. מדלא כתיב מן הבקר והצאן, משמע שניהם, דאתא לפרש מאיזו בהמה: מן הבקר ומן הצאן, מזה אחד ומזה אחד. ואף ע"ג דדרשי' בתמורה (דף כח:) כוליה, דוי"ו דידיה נמי דריש התם - מ"מ אי לא כתיב הכא או לחלק, הוה דרישנא ליה למימר דבעינא יחדו:
Tosafot on Menachot 91a:1:1.english: Since it is written: “And of the flock,” it is as though it is written: “Together” - For since it is written: “Of the cattle” [Leviticus 1:2] and it then writes: “Of the herd and of the flock,” this implies both (and in the Kuntres [Rashi] explained in a different way), as both phrases serve to explain “cattle.” Since it did not write: “Of the herd and the flock,” it implies both, for it comes to specify from which cattle: “Of the herd and of the flock” — one from this and one from that. And even though in Temurah (28b) we expound the entire phrase — for its vav is also expounded there [to exclude a goring animal] — nevertheless, had it not written here “or” to divide them, we would have expounded it to say that we require [both] together.
